title: Customer-anchored eval harness with private data gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a tenant-scoped eval harness that lets Dedicated and Private customers register private test suites and run model/config regressions without exposing raw customer data outside their VPC or to shared infra. The harness should tie into the existing eval pipeline but add strict data gating, encryption-at-rest, and an opt-in per-customer registry for eval artifacts.

Why: Many enterprise customers require the ability to run quality checks on pinned model versions and on rollout changes (quantization profiles, batching configs, kernel selections) but cannot send sensitive prompt/result pairs to a central eval fleet. This ticket defines the PM-level scope & acceptance criteria for a privacy-first customer eval feature that integrates with the Console and Release rollouts.

Key features (high level):
- Tenant-scoped eval suites: customers upload encrypted prompt sets and expected labels into a customer-owned S3/Vault or our on-prem artifact store.
- Local runner or VPC runner: Eval jobs can be executed inside the customer's Dedicated pool or Private deployment, ensuring no egress of raw inputs.
- Result aggregation only: Only metrics (accuracy, P95 latency, regressions flags, diffs of distributions) are sent to Redwood Console; raw texts are never transmitted unless explicitly allowed and consented.
- Config-change hooks: The harness runs automatically when model/config changes are staged (canary, rollout) and reports pass/fail to the rollout controller.
- Audit & cryptographic verification: Each run produces audit metadata signed by the runner; optional customer KMS to encrypt artifacts.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Running inside customer Dedicated/on-prem increases cost and scheduling complexity. We'll provide estimated cost templates and a lightweight runner first; a fully managed enclave will follow.
- To guarantee no data egress, some telemetry will need to be replaced by summarized metrics. This requires careful metric design to retain signal for regressions while avoiding sensitive leakage.
- We will reuse parts of the existing eval engine (eval-core) but must ensure it can compile to a VPC-friendly binary and satisfy minimal dependency footprint.

Phases & rollout plan:
1) Prototype (RFC + PoC, 2 sprints): Minimal runner that can execute a small eval suite inside a Dedicated pool; results stored in customer S3 and a signed metrics blob posted to Console. (Eng: containerized runner + auth).
2) Beta (3 sprints): Add Console UI for registering private suites, RBAC controls, and automated hooks into canary rollouts. Invite 3 enterprise customers.
3) GA: Harden security review outcomes, KMS integrations for BYOK, audit logs, and a clear pricing page.

Success metrics:
- 0 customers blocked from running evals for privacy reasons in beta cohort.
- False positive regression rate < 10% over first 30 days.
- Time-to-results for a standard 1k-example suite < 30 minutes on a Dedicated X pool.

Open questions (to decide in RFC):
- Storage model: customer-managed S3 vs Redwood-managed encrypted store for Private deployments.
- Metrics shape: which compressed metrics are sufficient to detect quality regressions without leaking tokens.
- RBAC granularity: who in the customer org can upload suites, view metrics, and approve rollouts.

- PoC PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-core/pull/412 (work in progress)
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/tenant-eval-summary

acceptance_criteria: Customer can register a private eval suite from Console and choose storage location (customer S3 or on-prem store)
Eval runner can execute in a Dedicated pool or Private deployment without sending raw inputs outside the customer's network
Console receives only signed metric blobs and displays regression summaries; no raw prompt/response visible by Redwood support unless explicitly granted
Automatic gate: a failing customer eval blocks canary promotion for that customer and logs an actionable reason
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for BYOK customers
